not_applicable_requirements_interpretati.rule_summary: This rule specifies behaviors or actions that are explicitly not allowed within the AFDX protocol.
not_applicable_requirements_interpretati.valid_range: Any behaviors or actions that are not explicitly prohibited by the protocol.

test_cases.value: Send data on a virtual link that is not provisioned
test_cases.reason: The protocol must not allow data transmission on a virtual link that has not been set up or defined in the network configuration.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network switch should drop the packet and log an error indicating an attempt to use an undefined virtual link.

test_cases.value: Use reserved field with non-zero value
test_cases.reason: Reserved fields are meant to remain zero or unused; non-zero values violate the protocol specifications.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The receiving system should ignore the message or flag it for error due to misuse of reserved fields.

test_cases.value: Transmit packets with a sequence number that does not increment
test_cases.reason: AFDX requires sequence numbers to increment to ensure packet order and integrity.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The receiver should detect the sequence error and possibly discard or reorder packets.

test_cases.value: Send packets exceeding the maximum frame size
test_cases.reason: Packets larger than the maximum allowed frame size violate the protocol's size constraints.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The switch should truncate the packet or drop it entirely, logging an error for oversized packet.

test_cases.value: Transmit packets at a rate exceeding the bandwidth allocation
test_cases.reason: Exceeding the allocated bandwidth violates the protocol's traffic-shaping requirements.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should throttle or drop excess packets to maintain network integrity.

test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject this value due to incorrect format and log an appropriate error.

test_cases.reason: Bandwidth should be an integer value, not a float.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject this value due to incorrect format and log an appropriate error.

latency.rule_summary: Latency must be bounded, ensuring data is delivered within a specific time frame.
latency.valid_range: Positive integers representing milliseconds or microseconds, within the acceptable range defined by system requirements.

test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject this value and possibly alert the user to configure within acceptable limits.

test_cases.reason: The format is incorrect as latency should be an integer value, not a string.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject this value due to incorrect format and log an appropriate error.

test_cases.reason: Latency should be an integer value, not a float.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject this value due to incorrect format and log an appropriate error.

Quality of Service.fault_isolation_in_sw.rule_summary: Switches must ensure fault isolation to prevent one end system's faults from affecting others.
Quality of Service.fault_isolation_in_sw.valid_range: Switches must isolate faults, ensuring a fault in one end system does not impact others.

test_cases.value: Switch allows broadcast of corrupted data
test_cases.reason: Corrupted data from one end system is broadcast to all end systems, violating isolation.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Switch should detect and contain the fault, dropping corrupted packets.

test_cases.value: Single point of failure in switch architecture
test_cases.reason: A design flaw where a single failure affects all connections violates fault isolation.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Switch should have redundancy to ensure one failure does not propagate.

test_cases.value: Switch forwards excessive traffic from one end system
test_cases.reason: Excessive traffic from one system overloads the switch, affecting all end systems.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Switch should throttle or block excessive traffic from a single source.

test_cases.reason: Incorrect VLAN configuration lets traffic spill over to unintended systems.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Switch should correctly segregate traffic based on VLAN tags.

test_cases.value: Switch firmware ignores fault isolation settings
test_cases.reason: A bug in firmware causes the switch to ignore isolation settings, letting faults spread.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Switch firmware should respect and enforce isolation settings strictly.

maximum_network_transit_delay_guarantee.rule_summary: Maximum network transit delay must be guaranteed for each transmission.
maximum_network_transit_delay_guarantee.valid_range: The network must ensure that all transmissions are completed within a specified maximum delay time, regardless of traffic conditions.

test_cases.reason: Introducing a traffic load that exceeds 100% of the network capacity can cause delays that exceed the guaranteed maximum transit delay.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should either throttle incoming requests or drop packets to maintain the delay guarantee.

test_cases.value: traffic_load: 99% of network capacity with sudden burst to 150%
test_cases.reason: A sudden burst of traffic beyond the network's capacity can temporarily overload the system, leading to delays exceeding the maximum transit delay.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should handle bursts gracefully, possibly through buffering or prioritization, to maintain the delay guarantee.

test_cases.value: constant high-priority traffic at 95% capacity with additional low-priority traffic
test_cases.reason: Overloading the network with high-priority traffic and additional low-priority traffic may cause delays in the processing of low-priority packets, exceeding guaranteed delays.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should enforce quality of service policies to ensure that all packets, regardless of priority, meet the delay requirements.

test_cases.value: multi-hop network with 90% capacity utilization per hop
test_cases.reason: Each hop introduces additional delay, and at high utilization, the cumulative delay across multiple hops can exceed the guaranteed maximum.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should optimize routing and minimize hops, or adjust the guaranteed delay to account for multi-hop scenarios.

test_cases.value: network failure recovery scenario causing rerouting
test_cases.reason: Network rerouting during failure recovery can introduce additional delays that may exceed the guaranteed transit delay.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should have rapid failover mechanisms to minimize delay during recovery scenarios.

test_cases.value: traffic prioritization incorrectly configured, causing low-priority traffic to delay high-priority traffic
test_cases.reason: Incorrect prioritization settings can lead to high-priority traffic being delayed by low-priority traffic, violating the maximum transit delay guarantee.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should detect misconfigurations and adjust prioritization settings to maintain delay guarantees.

test_cases.value: network congestion leading to packet queuing at maximum buffer capacity
test_cases.reason: Extreme congestion that fills buffers can cause packets to be queued longer than the guaranteed maximum delay.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should manage buffer usage effectively, possibly by dropping packets or using congestion control mechanisms.

guaranteed_bandwidth_requirement.rule_summary: Guaranteed service must provide constant bandwidth at link level
guaranteed_bandwidth_requirement.valid_range: Bandwidth should remain constant, ensuring both upper bounded delay and a logical open connection

test_cases.reason: Bandwidth allocation fluctuates over time instead of remaining constant, violating the guaranteed bandwidth requirement.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network switch should detect the fluctuation and possibly trigger an alert or error due to non-compliance.

test_cases.reason: No bandwidth is allocated, contradicting the requirement for a guaranteed constant bandwidth.
test_cases.expected_behavior: This should result in a failure to establish a logical open connection or trigger an error indicating insufficient resources.

test_cases.reason: Negative bandwidth allocation is nonsensical and violates the requirement for positive constant bandwidth.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject this configuration as invalid and raise an error.

test_cases.reason: A sudden spike in bandwidth followed by a drop disrupts the constant bandwidth requirement.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should identify this as a breach of the constant bandwidth rule and alert the administrator.

test_cases.reason: Periodic loss of bandwidth creates interruptions, violating the constant bandwidth provision.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should detect these interruptions and flag them as violations of the guaranteed service.

test_cases.reason: Requesting bandwidth beyond the physical link capacity breaches the constant bandwidth at feasible levels.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should deny the request or reallocate to feasible levels, possibly alerting about the excessive request.

minimum_reassembly_buffer_size.rule_summary: The minimum reassembly buffer size must be at least 576 bytes.
minimum_reassembly_buffer_size.valid_range: Values must be greater than or equal to 576.

test_cases.reason: The value is just below the minimum requirement of 576 bytes.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject this buffer size or raise an error indicating insufficient buffer size.

test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should handle this as an error and possibly halt the reassembly process.

test_cases.reason: Non-integer value, even though it rounds close to 576, it's not a valid integer size.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject non-integer buffer sizes, enforcing integer-only values.

test_cases.reason: Negative buffer sizes are non-sensical and violate the requirement of being at least 576 bytes.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should raise an error for negative buffer sizes and ensure no allocation is performed.

test_cases.reason: Negative buffer size of -576 directly contradicts the minimum positive requirement.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should treat this as an error and prevent reassembly using such a size.

test_cases.reason: Non-numeric format provided as a string, not a valid buffer size.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject this value with a type error, expecting a numeric input.

test_cases.reason: Floating-point number close to minimum but not an integer, not a valid buffer size.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should reject this input due to format constraints, expecting an integer size.

icmp_time_exceeded_on_reassembly_timeout.rule_summary: If reassembly timeout expires, discard datagram and send ICMP Time Exceeded
icmp_time_exceeded_on_reassembly_timeout.valid_range: Upon reassembly timeout, an ICMP Time Exceeded message should be sent

test_cases.value: No ICMP message sent upon timeout
test_cases.reason: The protocol specifies that an ICMP Time Exceeded message must be sent when a reassembly timeout occurs, so failing to send it violates the rule.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should detect that no ICMP message was sent and log an error or take corrective action.

test_cases.reason: Sending an ICMP Time Exceeded message before the timeout actually occurs contradicts the requirement to wait for the timeout.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should disregard the premature ICMP message and issue a proper one upon actual timeout.

test_cases.reason: Sending an ICMP message with a type other than 'Time Exceeded' does not comply with the rule's specification.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should recognize the incorrect ICMP type and potentially log or alert this misconfiguration.

test_cases.value: Time Exceeded message sent with incorrect code
test_cases.reason: The ICMP Time Exceeded message must have the correct code to indicate a reassembly timeout specifically.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should identify the incorrect code and log an error regarding the malformed ICMP message.

test_cases.value: Multiple ICMP messages sent for a single timeout
test_cases.reason: The rule specifies a single ICMP Time Exceeded message per timeout, so sending multiple violates protocol efficiency and correctness.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should ignore duplicate ICMP messages and ensure only one is processed.

test_cases.value: ICMP message sent with spoofed source IP
test_cases.reason: Sending an ICMP Time Exceeded message with a source IP that doesn't match the original sender can lead to security vulnerabilities.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should verify the source IP and reject or log the spoofed message.

test_cases.reason: Negative position value, which is not a valid identifier in the VL format.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The switch should reject this configuration as the position value must be non-negative.

test_cases.reason: Missing position value in the VL identifier, making it syntactically incorrect.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The switch should reject this configuration due to the incomplete VL identifier.

test_cases.reason: An unreasonably large position value that exceeds typical operational limits.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The switch should reject this configuration as it may lead to resource exhaustion or overflow issues.

test_cases.reason: Non-numeric position value, violating the expected numeric format for the position identifier.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The switch should reject this configuration due to the non-numeric position value.

test_cases.reason: Attempt to configure the switch with multiple subscriptions in a single configuration line.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The switch should only accept a single unique subscription and reject or ignore the others.

virtual_link_configuration.default_trans.rule_summary: Each switch must have a unique default transmission VL identifier.
virtual_link_configuration.default_trans.valid_range: Unique string identifiers for each switch's default transmission VL.

test_cases.reason: Two switches are configured with the same transmission VL 'VL(1,1)', violating the uniqueness requirement.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network switch should detect the duplicate and reject the configuration.

test_cases.reason: Three switches are configured with the same transmission VL 'VL(1,1)', thus violating the uniqueness rule.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should detect multiple duplicates and generate an error.

test_cases.reason: The VL identifier 'VL(1,-1)' contains a negative position, which is invalid.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should reject this configuration due to invalid format.

test_cases.reason: The VL identifier 'VL(1,999999999)' uses an extremely large number for position, likely exceeding typical limits.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should handle this gracefully, either by rejecting or capping the value.

test_cases.reason: The VL identifier 'VL(1,abc)' uses a non-numeric position, which is invalid.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should reject this configuration due to invalid format.

test_cases.reason: The VL identifier 'VL(,position)' is missing segments, making it invalid.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The network should reject this configuration due to incomplete format.

test_cases.reason: The VL identifier 'VL1position' does not follow the expected 'VL(1,position)' format.
test_cases.expected_behavior: The system should detect the format error and reject the configuration.
